hi.strong_distractor: d — विकल्प d (1, 2 और 3) एक मजबूत भ्रम है क्योंकि जो छात्र अरविंद और सावरकर को एक ही हिंदू राष्ट्रवादी परियोजना के दो रूप मानते हैं वे तीनों कथनों को स्वीकार कर सकते हैं, जिससे अरविंद के समावेशवाद के दावे और सावरकर के स्पष्ट जातीय बहिष्कार के बीच प्रलेखित भेद को समझना छूट जाता है।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 की पुष्टि करें: अरविंद और सावरकर दोनों क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवाद से उभरे और बाद में अलग हो गए — यह प्रलेखित और सही है।
कथन 2 को अस्वीकार करें: अरविंद ने स्पष्ट रूप से इनकार किया कि उनका हिंदू प्रतीकों का उपयोग जातीय-धार्मिक बहिष्कार के लिए था; इसे सावरकर के ढांचे के साथ जोड़ना गलत है — कथन 2 गलत है।
कथन 3 की पुष्टि करें: मुस्लिम नेताओं और धर्मनिरपेक्ष राष्ट्रवादियों की आलोचना प्रलेखित है कि हिंदू प्रतीकों के व्यावहारिक बहिष्कार प्रभाव थे — कथन 3 सही है।
केवल कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं — विकल्प (b)।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: यह भ्रम अरविंद के सभ्यतागत राष्ट्रवाद और सावरकर के हिंदुत्व के बीच है। दोनों हिंदू प्रतीकों का उपयोग करते हैं; दोनों क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवाद से निकले हैं। लेकिन अरविंद की स्पष्ट स्थिति एक समग्र सभ्यतागत पहचान थी जो धार्मिक विभाजनों से ऊपर थी, जबकि सावरकर का हिंदुत्व राष्ट्रीयता को हिंदू सांस्कृतिक वंशानुक्रम के माध्यम से परिभाषित करता है। कथन 2 छात्र को घोषित सार्वभौमिक उद्देश्य और व्यावहारिक बहिष्कार प्रभाव के बीच अंतर करने के लिए मजबूर करता है — एक सूक्ष्म भेद जो गहरी तैयारी की परीक्षा लेता है।
hi.final_explanation:
अरविंद के धार्मिक राष्ट्रवाद और सांप्रदायिक राजनीति के बीच संबंध भारतीय बौद्धिक इतिहास की सबसे सूक्ष्म बहसों में से एक है।

• कथन 1 — सही: अरविंद और सावरकर दोनों ब्रिटिश शासन के क्रांतिकारी विरोधी थे। उनकी राहें तीव्र रूप से अलग हुईं: सावरकर ने हिंदुत्व को एक स्पष्ट हिंदू-केंद्रित राष्ट्रवादी विचारधारा के रूप में विकसित किया; अरविंद के 1910 के बाद के लेखन ने भारत के सभी धार्मिक परंपराओं को समाहित करने वाली सार्वभौमिक आध्यात्मिक पहचान पर जोर दिया।
• कथन 2 — गलत: अरविंद ने अपने कार्य को जातीय बहिष्कार के रूप में वर्णित करने से स्पष्ट रूप से इनकार किया। उन्होंने दावा किया कि हिंदू दार्शनिक श्रेणियाँ — शक्ति, कर्म योग, सनातन धर्म — एक भारतीय सभ्यता की सार्वभौमिक शब्दावली हैं जिसमें मुसलमान और अन्य शामिल हैं। यह दावा कितना विश्वसनीय है, इस पर बहस है, लेकिन उनकी घोषित स्थिति सावरकर के स्पष्ट हिंदुत्व ढांचे से भिन्न है।
• कथन 3 — सही: आलोचना वास्तविक और प्रलेखित है। हिंदू देवी-देवताओं की छवि, संस्कृत दर्शन, और भगवद गीता को राष्ट्रवाद की मुख्य शब्दावली के रूप में उपयोग करने से अरविंद के ढांचे को कई मुस्लिम और धर्मनिरपेक्ष समकालीनों ने बहिष्कृत अनुभव किया, भले ही उनका सार्वभौमिक उद्देश्य था।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• सावरकर की 'हिंदुत्व: कौन हिंदू है?' (1923) ने राष्ट्र को हिंदू सभ्यतागत वंशानुक्रम के माध्यम से परिभाषित किया — एक मानदंड जो मुसलमानों और ईसाइयों को बाहर रखता है।
• पार्थ चटर्जी के 'राष्ट्रवाद के आंतरिक क्षेत्र' के विश्लेषण में आध्यात्मिक-सांस्कृतिक क्षेत्र को वह स्थान बताया गया है जहाँ हिंदू राष्ट्रवादियों ने अपनी ऊर्जा केंद्रित की।
• अरविंद के बाद के पांडिचेरी लेखन हिंदू-मुस्लिम एकता पर उनके पूर्व 1910 राजनीतिक चरण की तुलना में अधिक स्पष्ट सार्वभौमिकता दर्शाते हैं।

shared.concept_anchor: Father of Indian Unrest title — Tilak not Aurobindo

en.display_text:
The phrase 'Father of Indian Unrest' was coined by the British journalist Valentine Chirol in his 1910 work on Indian politics. Which Indian nationalist leader was this phrase specifically attributed to?

(a) Bipin Chandra Pal
(b) Lala Lajpat Rai
(c) Aurobindo Ghosh
(d) Bal Gangadhar Tilak
en.strong_distractor: c — Option c is a strong distractor because Aurobindo is often studied alongside Tilak as the intellectual mentor of revolutionary nationalism, and the 'Father of Indian Unrest' descriptor sounds more appropriate for a philosopher-provocateur like Aurobindo than for the politically active Tilak.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a): Bipin Chandra Pal is associated with spiritual nationalism and Bengal Extremism but the 'Father of Indian Unrest' title is not attributed to him by any standard historical source.
Eliminate option (b): Lala Lajpat Rai is associated with Punjab's nationalist movement and the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio but this specific title is not his.
Eliminate option (c): Aurobindo Ghosh is the ideological architect of revolutionary nationalism but the 'Father of Indian Unrest' is specifically Valentine Chirol's attribution to Tilak.

Confirm option (d): Valentine Chirol, the British journalist, coined the phrase 'Father of Indian Unrest' specifically for Bal Gangadhar Tilak in his 1910 book 'Indian Unrest' — Tilak subsequently sued Chirol for defamation.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The entity-swap trap works because both Aurobindo and Tilak are canonical Extremist leaders, and Aurobindo's role as the movement's intellectual architect makes the 'Father of Indian Unrest' label seem more fitting for him. In reality, it was coined by Valentine Chirol specifically for Tilak — the political organizer and mass mobilizer — and Tilak's response (suing Chirol for defamation in London) made the attribution famous. Students who know the phrase but not its precise attribution fall into this trap.
en.final_explanation:
The title 'Father of Indian Unrest' has a specific and documented origin in the literature of colonial political commentary.

• Option (a) Bipin Chandra Pal: A major Bengal Extremist leader and journalist, part of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio — but this title is not attributed to him.
• Option (b) Lala Lajpat Rai: The 'Lal' of the trio, associated with Punjab's nationalist movement — but this specific title is not his.
• Option (c) Aurobindo Ghosh: The primary ideological architect of revolutionary nationalism in Bengal — but the 'Father of Indian Unrest' is not his designation.
• Option (d) Bal Gangadhar Tilak: Correct. British journalist Valentine Chirol used this phrase in his 1910 book 'Indian Unrest' to describe Tilak's role in radicalizing Indian political sentiment. Tilak responded by suing Chirol for defamation in a London court — a case he lost.

Value Addition:
• Tilak's Mandalay imprisonment (1908–14) was a direct consequence of his Kesari writings deemed seditious.
• Tilak remained in active politics until his death in 1920; Aurobindo withdrew to Pondicherry in 1910.
• The Lucknow Pact (1916) marked Tilak's return to center-stage Congress politics after his release from Mandalay.

hi.display_text:
'फादर ऑफ इंडियन अनरेस्ट' शब्द ब्रिटिश पत्रकार वैलेंटाइन चिरोल ने 1910 में भारतीय राजनीति पर अपने कार्य में गढ़ा था। यह शब्द विशेष रूप से किस भारतीय राष्ट्रवादी नेता को दिया गया था?

(a) बिपिन चंद्र पाल
(b) लाला लाजपत राय
(c) आचार्य अरविंद घोष
(d) बाल गंगाधर तिलक
hi.strong_distractor: c — विकल्प c एक मजबूत भ्रम पैदा करने वाला है क्योंकि आचार्य अरविंद को अक्सर तिलक के साथ क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवाद के बौद्धिक गुरु के रूप में पढ़ाया जाता है, और 'फादर ऑफ इंडियन अनरेस्ट' उपाधि एक दार्शनिक-उत्तेजक के लिए अधिक उपयुक्त लगती है जैसे आचार्य अरविंद, न कि राजनीतिक रूप से सक्रिय तिलक के लिए।
elimination_logic: विकल्प (a) को निरस्त करें: बिपिन चंद्र पाल आध्यात्मिक राष्ट्रवाद और बंगाल उग्रवाद से जुड़े हैं लेकिन 'फादर ऑफ इंडियन अनरेस्ट' उपाधि किसी भी मानक ऐतिहासिक स्रोत द्वारा उन्हें नहीं दी गई है।
विकल्प (b) को निरस्त करें: लाला लाजपत राय पंजाब के राष्ट्रवादी आंदोलन और 'लाल-बल-पाल' त्रयी से जुड़े हैं लेकिन यह विशिष्ट उपाधि उनकी नहीं है।
विकल्प (c) को निरस्त करें: आचार्य अरविंद घोष क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवाद के वैचारिक वास्तुकार हैं लेकिन 'फादर ऑफ इंडियन अनरेस्ट' विशेष रूप से वैलेंटाइन चिरोल द्वारा तिलक को दी गई उपाधि है।

विकल्प (d) को पुष्टि करें: ब्रिटिश पत्रकार वैलेंटाइन चिरोल ने 1910 की अपनी पुस्तक 'Indian Unrest' में विशेष रूप से बाल गंगाधर तिलक के लिए 'फादर ऑफ इंडियन अनरेस्ट' शब्द गढ़ा था — तिलक ने बाद में चिरोल के खिलाफ मानहानि का मुकदमा लंदन में दायर किया था।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: यह एंटिटी-स्वैप जाल तब काम करता है क्योंकि आचार्य अरविंद और तिलक दोनों ही प्रमुख उग्रवादी नेता हैं, और आचार्य अरविंद की भूमिका इस आंदोलन के बौद्धिक वास्तुकार के रूप में 'फादर ऑफ इंडियन अनरेस्ट' उपाधि को उनके लिए अधिक उपयुक्त बनाती है। वास्तविकता में, यह उपाधि वैलेंटाइन चिरोल ने विशेष रूप से तिलक के लिए गढ़ी थी — जो राजनीतिक आयोजक और जन आंदोलनकर्ता थे — और तिलक की प्रतिक्रिया (चिरोल के खिलाफ लंदन में मानहानि का मुकदमा) ने इस उपाधि को प्रसिद्ध बना दिया। जो छात्र इस उपाधि को जानते हैं लेकिन इसके सटीक स्रोत को नहीं जानते, वे इस जाल में फंस जाते हैं।
hi.final_explanation:
'फादर ऑफ इंडियन अनरेस्ट' उपाधि का एक विशिष्ट और प्रलेखित स्रोत है जो औपनिवेशिक राजनीतिक टिप्पणी की साहित्य में मिलता है।

• विकल्प (a) बिपिन चंद्र पाल: बंगाल के प्रमुख उग्रवादी नेता और पत्रकार, 'लाल-बल-पाल' त्रयी के सदस्य — लेकिन यह उपाधि उन्हें नहीं दी गई।
• विकल्प (b) लाला लाजपत राय: त्रयी के 'लाल', पंजाब के राष्ट्रवादी आंदोलन से जुड़े — लेकिन यह विशिष्ट उपाधि उनकी नहीं है।
• विकल्प (c) आचार्य अरविंद घोष: बंगाल में क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवाद के मुख्य वैचारिक वास्तुकार — लेकिन 'फादर ऑफ इंडियन अनरेस्ट' उनकी उपाधि नहीं है।
• विकल्प (d) बाल गंगाधर तिलक: सही। ब्रिटिश पत्रकार वैलेंटाइन चिरोल ने 1910 की अपनी पुस्तक 'Indian Unrest' में तिलक की भूमिका को भारतीय राजनीतिक भावना को उग्र करने वाला बताते हुए यह शब्द इस्तेमाल किया। तिलक ने लंदन की अदालत में चिरोल के खिलाफ मानहानि का मुकदमा दायर किया, जो वे हार गए।

मूल्यवर्धन:
• तिलक का मंडले जेलवास (1908–14) उनके केशरी लेखों को देशद्रोही मानने के कारण हुआ था।
• तिलक 1920 में अपनी मृत्यु तक सक्रिय राजनीति में रहे; आचार्य अरविंद 1910 में पांडिचेरी चले गए।
• लखनऊ संधि (1916) तिलक की मंडले से रिहाई के बाद कांग्रेस राजनीति में वापसी थी।

en.display_text:
With reference to Aurobindo Ghosh's Pondicherry phase (1910–1950), consider the following statements:

1. Aurobindo Ghosh was entirely apolitical during his Pondicherry phase and maintained complete silence on Indian political developments, including the Independence movement and Partition.
2. Indian independence on August 15, 1947 coincided with Aurobindo Ghosh's seventy-fifth birthday, an event he publicly acknowledged in a radio address articulating his vision for the newly independent nation.
3. Scholars debate whether Aurobindo's post-1910 Pondicherry phase represented a complete rupture with his earlier political nationalism or a philosophical deepening and continuation of the same civilizational project by different means.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Aurobindo Ghosh was entirely apolitical during his Pondicherry phase (1910–1950) and maintained complete silence on Indian political developments, including the Independence movement and Partition.
statement_analysis.reason: Aurobindo continued to correspond on political matters and made public statements during the 1920s–40s; his radio address on August 15, 1947 articulating a vision for independent India is evidence that he was not entirely silent on political matters even during his Pondicherry years.

statement_analysis.statement: Indian independence on August 15, 1947 coincided with Aurobindo Ghosh's seventy-fifth birthday, an event he publicly acknowledged in a radio address articulating his vision for the newly independent nation.
statement_analysis.reason: Aurobindo was born on August 15, 1872; Indian independence on August 15, 1947 thus fell on his 75th birthday — a coincidence he acknowledged publicly and which he saw as spiritually significant.

statement_analysis.statement: Scholars debate whether Aurobindo's post-1910 Pondicherry phase represented a complete rupture with his earlier political nationalism or a philosophical deepening and continuation of the same civilizational project by different means.
statement_analysis.reason: This is an established historiographical debate: some scholars emphasize continuity (the spiritual and political phases as parts of one integrated vision of India's liberation and civilizational destiny), while others emphasize the rupture (withdrawal from active politics as an abandonment of the revolutionary project).

en.strong_distractor: a — Option a (1 and 2 only) is a strong distractor because students who know Aurobindo's famous August 15 connection accept Statement 2, and may not scrutinize Statement 1 carefully enough to catch the 'entirely apolitical' and 'complete silence' overstatements.
elimination_logic: Reject Statement 1: The qualifier 'entirely apolitical' and 'complete silence' are scope-extension errors — Aurobindo made political statements including his 1947 radio address. Statement 1 is Incorrect.
Confirm Statement 2: August 15, 1947 was Aurobindo's 75th birthday; his radio address on that date is documented. Statement 2 is Correct.
Confirm Statement 3: The continuity vs. rupture debate about Aurobindo's Pondicherry phase is a recognized historiographical discussion. Statement 3 is Correct.
Only Statements 2 and 3 are correct — option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 1 is a scope-extension trap. Students may have a general impression that Aurobindo 'withdrew from politics' in Pondicherry — which is broadly true as a description of his primary focus — and then accept the amplified version 'entirely apolitical' and 'complete silence' without checking the qualifier. The August 15, 1947 radio address alone is sufficient to falsify the absolute claim in Statement 1.
en.final_explanation:
Aurobindo's Pondicherry phase is often simplified as a complete withdrawal from politics into spirituality. The reality is more nuanced.

• Statement 1 — Incorrect: 'Entirely apolitical' and 'complete silence' are overstatements. Aurobindo continued to express political views through correspondence and public statements during the 1920s–40s. His August 15, 1947 radio address — delivered on the day of Indian independence — articulated a vision for India that encompassed political, cultural, and spiritual dimensions.
• Statement 2 — Correct: Aurobindo was born on August 15, 1872. Indian independence on August 15, 1947 thus fell exactly on his 75th birthday — a coincidence he found spiritually meaningful and publicly acknowledged in a radio broadcast where he outlined five dreams for India and humanity.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Historians genuinely debate whether the Pondicherry phase represents rupture (abandonment of the revolutionary project) or continuity (the same civilizational liberation pursued through deeper philosophical means). Both interpretive positions have scholarly support.

Value Addition:
• Aurobindo's five dreams articulated in the 1947 radio address included: a united India, Asian resurgence, world unity, a spiritual gift from India, and the evolution of human consciousness.
• The Sri Aurobindo Ashram in Pondicherry became an internationally recognized centre of integral yoga.
• Aurobindo died on December 5, 1950 — shortly after India became a Republic.

Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R):

Assertion (A): Aurobindo Ghosh articulated the demand for complete independence — not Dominion Status — as the only acceptable political goal for India as early as 1906–07, predating the Indian National Congress's formal adoption of Purna Swaraj by over two decades.

Reason (R): The Indian National Congress at its Lahore session in December 1929, under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, formally adopted Purna Swaraj as the national goal and declared January 26 as Independence Day.

(a) Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) A is incorrect but R is correct
en.strong_distractor: a — Option a is a strong distractor because students who know both claims are factually true may assume that Aurobindo's prior articulation of Purna Swaraj logically explains why the 1929 Congress passed the resolution — missing that the 1929 resolution emerged from its own political context (Simon Commission, Nehru Report) and was not caused by Aurobindo's 1906–07 writings.
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is Assertion (A) correct? — Yes. Aurobindo articulated the demand for complete independence (Purna Swaraj) as early as 1906–07, over two decades before the Congress's formal 1929 Lahore resolution.
Step 2: Is Reason (R) correct? — Yes. The 1929 Lahore Congress under Nehru's presidency did formally adopt Purna Swaraj as the national goal, rejecting Dominion Status.

Step 3: Does R causally explain A? — No. The 1929 Congress resolution was driven by the failure of the Nehru Report, the Simon Commission boycott, and the political dynamics of 1928–29 — not by Aurobindo's 1906–07 writings. R states a true fact that happened after A but does not explain why A occurred.
A correct + R correct + R does NOT explain A → option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The temporal-swap trap is embedded in the causal relationship. Students who know both facts — Aurobindo's early Purna Swaraj demand and the 1929 Congress resolution — may construct a false causal chain: 'Aurobindo said it first, therefore that's why Congress adopted it.' In reality, the 1929 Lahore resolution had its own immediate political causes (Simon Commission, Nehru Report failure, rising mass nationalism) and was not caused by Aurobindo's writings, even if those writings showed prescient alignment. The Reason is a true fact that is chronologically after A but causally unconnected to A.
en.final_explanation:
Aurobindo's intellectual pioneering on Purna Swaraj and the Congress's 1929 formal adoption are both factual — but connecting them causally requires examining the actual historical context of each.

Assertion (A): Correct. Aurobindo articulated complete independence (not Dominion Status) as the only acceptable goal of Indian nationalism as early as 1906–07. This placed him well ahead of the mainstream Congress position, which remained ambiguous about Dominion Status vs. full independence until 1929.

Reason (R): Correct. The Lahore Congress of December 1929 under Jawaharlal Nehru's presidency formally adopted Purna Swaraj as the national goal, rejecting the Dominion Status offer. January 26, 1930 was declared Independence Day.

Causal link: R does not explain A. The 1929 resolution was caused by the rejection of the Nehru Report by the British and Muslim League, the Simon Commission crisis, and rising nationalist pressure — not by Aurobindo's 1906–07 writings. A is true; R is true; but R is not the explanation for A.

This maps to option (b).

Value Addition:
• The Nehru Report (1928) had proposed Dominion Status; its rejection by both British authorities and the Muslim League accelerated the 1929 Purna Swaraj resolution.
• January 26 was chosen as Republic Day (1950) to commemorate the 1930 Independence Day pledge.
• Bhagat Singh, influenced by Aurobindo's revolutionary nationalism ideologically, also demanded full independence and rejected constitutional gradualism.

hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कालानुक्रमिक-परिवर्तन (temporal-swap) जाल कारणात्मक संबंध में निहित है। जो छात्र दोनों तथ्यों — औरोबिंदो की प्रारंभिक पूर्ण स्वराज मांग और 1929 के कांग्रेस प्रस्ताव — को जानते हैं, वे एक गलत कारणात्मक श्रृंखला बना सकते हैं: 'औरोबिंदो ने पहले कहा, इसलिए कांग्रेस ने इसे अपनाया।' वास्तविकता में, 1929 का लाहौर प्रस्ताव अपने तत्काल राजनीतिक कारणों (साइमन कमीशन, नेहरू रिपोर्ट की विफलता, बढ़ता राष्ट्रवाद) से प्रेरित था और औरोबिंदो के लेखन से प्रेरित नहीं था, भले ही वे विचारधारात्मक रूप से मेल खाते हों। कारण (R) एक सत्य तथ्य है जो कालानुक्रम में A के बाद है पर कारणात्मक रूप से उससे असंबंधित है।
hi.final_explanation:
औरोबिंदो का पूर्ण स्वराज पर बौद्धिक नेतृत्व और कांग्रेस का 1929 में औपचारिक स्वीकृति दोनों तथ्यात्मक रूप से सही हैं — लेकिन उन्हें कारणात्मक रूप से जोड़ने के लिए प्रत्येक के ऐतिहासिक संदर्भ की जांच आवश्यक है।

कथन (A): सही। औरोबिंदो ने 1906–07 में ही पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता (डोमिनियन स्टेटस नहीं) को भारतीय राष्ट्रवाद का एकमात्र स्वीकार्य लक्ष्य बताया, जो कांग्रेस की उस समय की अस्पष्ट स्थिति से बहुत आगे था।

कारण (R): सही। 1929 के दिसंबर में जवाहरलाल नेहरू की अध्यक्षता में लाहौर कांग्रेस ने पूर्ण स्वराज को राष्ट्रीय लक्ष्य के रूप में अपनाया और डोमिनियन स्टेटस को अस्वीकार किया। 26 जनवरी 1930 को स्वतंत्रता दिवस घोषित किया गया।

कारणात्मक संबंध: R, A को समझाता नहीं है। 1929 का प्रस्ताव नेहरू रिपोर्ट के ब्रिटिश और मुस्लिम लीग द्वारा अस्वीकृति, साइमन कमीशन संकट, और बढ़ते राष्ट्रवादी दबाव से प्रेरित था — न कि औरोबिंदो के 1906–07 के लेखन से। A सत्य है; R सत्य है; पर R, A का कारण नहीं है।

यह विकल्प (b) से मेल खाता है।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• नेहरू रिपोर्ट (1928) ने डोमिनियन स्टेटस का प्रस्ताव किया था; इसे ब्रिटिश और मुस्लिम लीग दोनों ने अस्वीकार किया, जिससे 1929 का पूर्ण स्वराज प्रस्ताव तेज़ हुआ।
• 26 जनवरी को गणतंत्र दिवस (1950) के रूप में चुना गया ताकि 1930 के स्वतंत्रता दिवस की प्रतिज्ञा को याद किया जा सके।
• भगत सिंह, जो औरोबिंदो के क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवाद से प्रेरित थे, उन्होंने भी पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता की मांग की और संवैधानिक क्रमिकता को अस्वीकार किया।

table_data.header_text: With reference to British legal repression of revolutionary nationalism and Aurobindo Ghosh's legal encounters, consider the following statements:
rows: Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code (sedition) was the primary legal instrument used against Aurobindo Ghosh, who faced multiple charges under this provision.

Regulation III of 1818, which allowed detention without trial, was used to secure Aurobindo's imprisonment during the Alipore case — making his acquittal legally impossible under the regulation's terms.
Aurobindo's acquittal in the Alipore case was, ironically, a setback for British strategy — his courtroom vindication amplified revolutionary sentiment and turned him into a national symbol.

British legal strategy systematically used deportation without trial under Regulation III of 1818 against several revolutionary leaders, though Aurobindo's acquittal through regular judicial process was exceptional among high-profile revolutionary cases.

(a) Only one
(b) Only two
(c) Only three

statement_analysis.statement: Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code (sedition) was the primary legal instrument used against Aurobindo Ghosh, who faced multiple charges under this provision.
statement_analysis.reason: Section 124A IPC (sedition) was the British colonial government's primary tool against revolutionary nationalists including Aurobindo, who faced sedition charges in connection with his revolutionary journalism and organizational activities.

statement_analysis.statement: Regulation III of 1818, which allowed detention without trial, was used to secure Aurobindo's imprisonment during the Alipore case — making his acquittal legally impossible under the regulation's terms.
statement_analysis.reason: Aurobindo was tried through the regular criminal court process in the Alipore case, not detained under Regulation III of 1818. The Regulation was used against other detainees (notably Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1897 and later political prisoners) but Aurobindo's Alipore case went through ordinary judicial process, resulting in acquittal — which would have been impossible under Regulation III's executive detention framework.

statement_analysis.statement: Aurobindo's acquittal in the Alipore case was, ironically, a setback for British strategy — his courtroom vindication amplified revolutionary sentiment and turned him into a national symbol.
statement_analysis.reason: Chittaranjan Das's celebrated defense and Aurobindo's acquittal transformed the trial into a platform for revolutionary nationalism; his release made him a national hero and amplified the movement's appeal rather than suppressing it.

statement_analysis.statement: British legal strategy systematically used deportation without trial under Regulation III of 1818 against several revolutionary leaders, though Aurobindo's acquittal through regular judicial process was exceptional among high-profile revolutionary cases.
statement_analysis.reason: Regulation III of 1818 was indeed used to deport and detain leaders without trial in high-profile cases (including Tilak in 1897, later Lokmanya Tilak again, and others), while Aurobindo uniquely went through a full judicial process and was acquitted — an exceptional outcome that demonstrated both the limits of British legal strategy and Chittaranjan Das's legal brilliance.

en.strong_distractor: c — Option c (Only three) is the correct answer, and option (b) (Only two) is the strong distractor for students who incorrectly accept Statement 2's claim about Regulation III being used in Aurobindo's Alipore case.
elimination_logic: Confirm Statement 1: Section 124A IPC as the primary sedition tool against Aurobindo is well-documented — Correct.

Reject Statement 2: Aurobindo's Alipore case used ordinary criminal court procedure — Regulation III of 1818 was an executive detention mechanism used elsewhere, not in the Alipore case. The claim that acquittal was 'legally impossible' under the regulation is also factually wrong — Statement 2 is Incorrect.
Confirm Statement 3: Aurobindo's acquittal amplifying revolutionary sentiment rather than suppressing it is documented — Correct.
Confirm Statement 4: Regulation III of 1818 was used against other revolutionary leaders, and Aurobindo's acquittal through regular judicial process was exceptional — Correct.
Three statements (1, 3, 4) are correct — option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 is a plausible fabrication. Students know Regulation III of 1818 was a real colonial instrument of repression and know Aurobindo was imprisoned — the statement sounds authoritative because it correctly names both the regulation and the case. The fabricated element is the claim that it was used in the Alipore case; it was not. Aurobindo went through ordinary criminal court proceedings, which is why acquittal was possible. A student without precise knowledge of the legal mechanism used in the Alipore case will accept Statement 2.
en.final_explanation:
British legal strategy against revolutionary nationalism combined ordinary criminal law (Section 124A IPC sedition) with exceptional executive detention (Regulation III of 1818), deploying them selectively.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Section 124A IPC was the primary sedition provision used against journalists and organizers like Aurobindo.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: The Alipore case proceeded through the ordinary criminal court system — this is why Aurobindo could be acquitted. Regulation III of 1818 was an executive detention mechanism that bypassed the courts entirely; had it been used, judicial acquittal would indeed have been impossible — but it was not used in the Alipore case.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The Alipore acquittal backfired for British authorities. Chittaranjan Das's closing argument ('In the prisoner... India of the future takes shape') and Aurobindo's release made him a national hero, amplifying the revolutionary movement's appeal.
• Statement 4 — Correct: Regulation III of 1818 was used against other leaders (Tilak in 1897 faced a related but distinct legal process); Aurobindo's full criminal trial and acquittal was exceptional in the landscape of British repression of revolutionary nationalism.

Value Addition:
• Section 124A IPC (sedition) was enacted by Thomas Macaulay and used extensively against Indian nationalists including Tilak, Gandhi, and Aurobindo.
• The Alipore case was also called the Manicktola Bomb Conspiracy Case.
• Regulation III of 1818 was finally repealed only in 1950 after Indian independence.

table_data.header_text: ब्रिटिश कानूनी दमन और ऑरोबिंदो घोष के कानूनी मुकदमों के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:
rows: भारतीय दंड संहिता की धारा 124A (राजद्रोह) ऑरोबिंदो घोष के खिलाफ प्रयुक्त प्राथमिक कानूनी उपकरण था, जिनके खिलाफ इस प्रावधान के तहत कई आरोप लगाए गए।

1818 के विनियमन III, जो बिना मुकदमे के हिरासत की अनुमति देता था, का उपयोग ऑरोबिंदो की गिरफ्तारी सुनिश्चित करने के लिए अलिपोर मामले में किया गया था — जिससे इस विनियमन की शर्तों के तहत उनकी बरी होना कानूनी रूप से असंभव था।
अलिपोर मामले में ऑरोबिंदो की बरी होना, विडंबना यह है कि, ब्रिटिश रणनीति के लिए एक असफलता थी — उनके न्यायालय में सफाई ने क्रांतिकारी भावना को बढ़ावा दिया और उन्हें एक राष्ट्रीय प्रतीक बना दिया।

hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 एक संभावित मिथ्या है। छात्र जानते हैं कि 1818 का विनियमन III एक वास्तविक औपनिवेशिक दमन उपकरण था और जानते हैं कि ऑरोबिंदो को जेल भी जाना पड़ा था — यह कथन प्राधिकृत लगता है क्योंकि यह विनियमन और मामले दोनों का सही नाम देता है। मिथ्या तत्व यह दावा है कि इसका उपयोग अलिपोर मामले में किया गया था; ऐसा नहीं था। ऑरोबिंदो सामान्य आपराधिक न्यायालय प्रक्रिया से गुजरे, इसलिए बरी होना संभव था। जो छात्र अलिपोर मामले में प्रयुक्त कानूनी तंत्र के बारे में सटीक जानकारी नहीं रखते, वे कथन 2 को स्वीकार कर लेंगे।
hi.final_explanation:
ब्रिटिश कानूनी रणनीति ने क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवाद के खिलाफ सामान्य आपराधिक कानून (धारा 124A IPC राजद्रोह) को असाधारण कार्यकारी हिरासत (1818 का विनियमन III) के साथ संयोजित किया, और इन्हें चयनात्मक रूप से लागू किया।

• कथन 1 — सही: धारा 124A IPC पत्रकारों और आयोजकों जैसे ऑरोबिंदो के खिलाफ मुख्य राजद्रोह प्रावधान था।
• कथन 2 — गलत: अलिपोर मामला सामान्य आपराधिक न्यायालय प्रणाली के माध्यम से चला — इसलिए ऑरोबिंदो बरी हो सके। 1818 का विनियमन III एक कार्यकारी हिरासत तंत्र था जो पूरी तरह से न्यायालयों को दरकिनार करता था; यदि इसका उपयोग हुआ होता, तो न्यायिक बरी असंभव होती — लेकिन इसका उपयोग अलिपोर मामले में नहीं हुआ।
• कथन 3 — सही: अलिपोर में बरी होना ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों के लिए उल्टा पड़ा। चित्तरंजन दास के समापन तर्क ('कैदी में... भारत का भविष्य आकार लेता है') और ऑरोबिंदो की रिहाई ने उन्हें राष्ट्रीय नायक बना दिया, जिससे क्रांतिकारी आंदोलन की अपील बढ़ी।
• कथन 4 — सही: 1818 का विनियमन III अन्य नेताओं के खिलाफ इस्तेमाल किया गया (1897 में तिलक ने संबंधित लेकिन भिन्न कानूनी प्रक्रिया का सामना किया); ऑरोबिंदो का पूर्ण आपराधिक परीक्षण और बरी होना ब्रिटिश दमन के परिदृश्य में असाधारण था।

मूल्यवर्धन:
• धारा 124A IPC (राजद्रोह) थॉमस मैकाले द्वारा लागू की गई थी और तिलक, गांधी, और ऑरोबिंदो सहित भारतीय राष्ट्रवादियों के खिलाफ व्यापक रूप से इस्तेमाल की गई।
• अलिपोर मामला को माणिकटोला बम साजिश मामला भी कहा जाता है।
• 1818 का विनियमन III अंततः भारतीय स्वतंत्रता के बाद 1950 में ही निरस्त किया गया।

en.strong_distractor: b — Option b is a strong distractor because students may associate Bipin Chandra (historian) with the nationalist school and Partha Chatterjee with a generically 'critical' school, and may swap their specific analytical contributions without knowing that Chatterjee's 'inner/outer domain' is the specific Subaltern Studies framework applicable here.
elimination_logic: Anchor A-3: Bipin Chandra (historian) assessed Aurobindo as the most important intellectual of the Extremist school who provided coherent ideology — a positive nationalist-school evaluation. Matches description 3.
Anchor B-1: R.P. Dutt's Marxist critique argued that Aurobindo's spiritualization of politics deflected from class-based analysis — matches description 1.

Anchor C-2: Partha Chatterjee's Subaltern Studies framework introduced the 'inner/outer domain' distinction — Aurobindo exemplifies the inner spiritual domain that nationalists prioritized. Matches description 2.
Anchor D-4: Post-colonial reassessment has debated continuity vs. rupture in Aurobindo's political-to-spiritual transition — matches description 4. Confirming option (d).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The entity-swap trap is between Bipin Chandra (historian, nationalist school) and Partha Chatterjee (Subaltern Studies). Both have written on Aurobindo but from sharply different frameworks. Students who know both names without being able to match them to their specific frameworks will swap A and C. Additionally, confusing R.P. Dutt's Marxist critique with a generic 'criticism of religion in politics' may cause students to misplace description 1.
en.final_explanation:
Aurobindo Ghosh has been assessed differently by distinct historiographical schools, and matching the school to its specific analytical contribution tests precision.

Correct Matches:
• A-3: Bipin Chandra (the historian, distinct from Bipin Chandra Pal the politician) placed Aurobindo at the apex of the Extremist school's intellectual output, arguing he gave revolutionary nationalism a coherent theoretical foundation.
• B-1: R.P. Dutt, writing from a Marxist perspective, criticized Aurobindo's spiritualization of nationalism as a deflection from the class contradictions that colonial exploitation created — religion as a substitute for class analysis.
• C-2: Partha Chatterjee's Subaltern Studies framework introduced the 'inner domain' (spiritual, cultural) vs. 'outer domain' (political, economic) distinction in colonial nationalism. Aurobindo is the paradigmatic example of a nationalist who concentrated nationalist energies in the inner spiritual domain.
• D-4: Post-colonial scholarship has debated whether Aurobindo's Pondicherry withdrawal represents a rupture from or continuity with his earlier political nationalism — a framing that cuts across all three schools.

Value Addition:
• Bipin Chandra (historian) co-authored 'India's Struggle for Independence' — a foundational nationalist-school text.
• Partha Chatterjee's 'Nationalist Thought and the Colonial World' (1986) is the seminal Subaltern Studies treatment of this theme.
• R.P. Dutt's 'India Today' (1940) offers the classic Marxist critique of Indian nationalism's spiritual turn.

hi.final_explanation:
ऑरोबिंदो घोष का विभिन्न इतिहासलेखन स्कूलों द्वारा अलग-अलग मूल्यांकन किया गया है, और स्कूल को उसके विशिष्ट विश्लेषणात्मक योगदान से मिलाना सटीकता की परीक्षा है।

सही मिलान:
• A-3: बिपिन चंद्र (इतिहासकार, बिपिन चंद्र पाल से भिन्न) ने ऑरोबिंदो को अतिवादी स्कूल की बौद्धिक उपलब्धि के शिखर पर रखा, यह तर्क देते हुए कि उन्होंने क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवाद को सुसंगत सैद्धांतिक आधार दिया।
• B-1: आर.पी. दत्त ने मार्क्सवादी दृष्टिकोण से लिखा, और ऑरोबिंदो के राष्ट्रवाद के आध्यात्मीकरण की आलोचना की क्योंकि यह उपनिवेशी शोषण से उत्पन्न वर्ग विरोधाभासों से ध्यान भटकाने वाला था — धर्म को वर्ग विश्लेषण के विकल्प के रूप में देखा।
• C-2: पार्थ चटर्जी के सबाल्टर्न स्टडीज ढांचे ने उपनिवेशी राष्ट्रवाद में 'आंतरिक क्षेत्र' (आध्यात्मिक, सांस्कृतिक) और 'बाह्य क्षेत्र' (राजनीतिक, आर्थिक) का भेद प्रस्तुत किया। ऑरोबिंदो उस राष्ट्रवादी का आदर्श उदाहरण हैं जिन्होंने राष्ट्रवादी ऊर्जा को आंतरिक आध्यात्मिक क्षेत्र में केंद्रित किया।
• D-4: उपनिवेशोत्तर विद्वता ने बहस की है कि क्या ऑरोबिंदो का पांडिचेरी वापसी उनका राजनीतिक राष्ट्रवाद से एक मौलिक विराम है या निरंतरता — यह दृष्टिकोण तीनों स्कूलों को पार करता है।

मूल्यवर्धन:
• बिपिन चंद्र (इतिहासकार) ने 'India's Struggle for Independence' की सह-रचना की — जो एक मौलिक राष्ट्रवादी-स्कूल ग्रंथ है।
• पार्थ चटर्जी की 'Nationalist Thought and the Colonial World' (1986) इस विषय पर सबाल्टर्न स्टडीज का महत्वपूर्ण ग्रंथ है।
• आर.पी. दत्त की 'India Today' (1940) भारतीय राष्ट्रवाद के आध्यात्मिक मोड़ की क्लासिक मार्क्सवादी आलोचना प्रस्तुत करती है।

en.display_text:
The Muzaffarpur bomb attempt of April 1908, which targeted a British district magistrate known for harsh sentences against Indian political activists, was directly carried out by which pair of revolutionaries?

(a) Aurobindo Ghosh and Barindra Kumar Ghosh
(b) Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki
(c) Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Narendra Nath Goswami
(d) Narendra Nath Goswami and Khudiram Bose
en.strong_distractor: c — Option c is a strong distractor because students who associate the Muzaffarpur bomb case with Aurobindo's Alipore trial may substitute Aurobindo's name for the actual perpetrators, or may know Barindra's connection without knowing the specific individuals involved in the Muzaffarpur attempt.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a): Aurobindo Ghosh was arrested in connection with the conspiracy but was not involved in the Muzaffarpur bomb attempt itself — his role was ideological and organizational.
Eliminate option (c): Barindra Kumar Ghosh was the operational leader of the Yugantar group but was not the person who carried out the Muzaffarpur attempt — Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki were.
Eliminate option (d): Narendra Nath Goswami became the government approver in the Alipore case — he was not involved in the Muzaffarpur attack.

Confirm option (b): Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki carried out the Muzaffarpur bomb attempt targeting the British judge Kingsford in April 1908 — Prafulla Chaki shot himself to avoid capture, and Khudiram Bose was arrested and subsequently executed.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The entity-swap trap substitutes Barindra Kumar Ghosh (the operational leader of the revolutionary group) for Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki (who actually carried out the Muzaffarpur attempt). Students who study the Alipore case in broad strokes know Barindra was convicted but may not separately anchor the Muzaffarpur perpetrators. This is also a test of whether students know Prafulla Chaki died by suicide rather than being captured.
en.final_explanation:
The Muzaffarpur bomb case (April 1908) is the event that triggered the mass arrests leading to the Alipore conspiracy trial.

• Option (a): Incorrect. Aurobindo was the ideological architect and organizational figure — he was arrested in the subsequent crackdown but did not participate in the Muzaffarpur attempt.
• Option (b): Correct. Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki carried out the Muzaffarpur bomb attempt, targeting the British district magistrate Kingsford who had earned notoriety for harsh sentences against political activists. The bomb inadvertently killed two British women instead. Prafulla Chaki died by suicide when cornered; Khudiram Bose was arrested and hanged in August 1908.
• Option (c): Incorrect. Barindra Kumar Ghosh directed the Yugantar group's activities but was not personally involved in the Muzaffarpur attack; he was convicted in the Alipore case for conspiracy.
• Option (d): Incorrect. Narendra Nath Goswami turned approver for the British prosecution in the Alipore case — he was assassinated by fellow revolutionaries inside the jail.

Value Addition:
• Khudiram Bose was approximately 18 years old at the time of his execution — one of India's youngest revolutionary martyrs.
• Kingsford was targeted because of his role as Chief Presidency Magistrate who had ordered the flogging of political prisoners.
• The Muzaffarpur bomb was made at the Manicktola garden house associated with Barindra's Yugantar group.

elimination_logic: (a) विकल्प को हटाएं: आरोबिंदो घोष साजिश के संबंध में गिरफ्तार हुए थे लेकिन मुजफ्फरपुर बम प्रयास में शामिल नहीं थे — उनकी भूमिका वैचारिक और संगठनात्मक थी।
(c) विकल्प को हटाएं: बरींद्र कुमार घोष युगांतर समूह के परिचालन नेता थे लेकिन मुजफ्फरपुर प्रयास को अंजाम देने वाले व्यक्ति नहीं थे — खुदीराम बोस और प्रफुल्ल चाकी थे।
(d) विकल्प को हटाएं: नरेंद्र नाथ गोस्वामी अलीपुर मामले में सरकार के गवाह बने थे — वे मुजफ्फरपुर हमले में शामिल नहीं थे।

(b) विकल्प की पुष्टि करें: खुदीराम बोस और प्रफुल्ल चाकी ने अप्रैल 1908 में ब्रिटिश न्यायाधीश किंग्सफोर्ड को निशाना बनाकर मुजफ्फरपुर बम प्रयास किया — प्रफुल्ल चाकी ने गिरफ्तारी से बचने के लिए आत्महत्या कर ली, और खुदीराम बोस को गिरफ्तार कर फांसी दी गई।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: सत्ता-वस्तु परिवर्तन (entity-swap) जाल में बरींद्र कुमार घोष (जो क्रांतिकारी समूह के परिचालन नेता थे) को खुदीराम बोस और प्रफुल्ल चाकी (जिन्होंने वास्तव में मुजफ्फरपुर प्रयास किया) के स्थान पर रखा जाता है। जो छात्र अलीपुर मामले को सामान्य रूप से पढ़ते हैं, वे जानते हैं कि बरींद्र दोषी ठहराए गए थे लेकिन मुजफ्फरपुर के अपराधियों को अलग से नहीं जानते। यह यह भी जांचता है कि छात्र जानते हैं कि प्रफुल्ल चाकी आत्महत्या करके मरा था, न कि पकड़ा गया था।
hi.final_explanation:
मुजफ्फरपुर बम मामला (अप्रैल 1908) वह घटना है जिसने अलीपुर साजिश मुकदमे के लिए व्यापक गिरफ्तारी शुरू की।

• विकल्प (a): गलत। आरोबिंदो वैचारिक वास्तुकार और संगठनात्मक नेता थे — वे बाद की कार्रवाई में गिरफ्तार हुए लेकिन मुजफ्फरपुर प्रयास में शामिल नहीं थे।
• विकल्प (b): सही। खुदीराम बोस और प्रफुल्ल चाकी ने मुजफ्फरपुर बम प्रयास किया, जिसका लक्ष्य ब्रिटिश जिला मजिस्ट्रेट किंग्सफोर्ड था, जो राजनीतिक कार्यकर्ताओं के खिलाफ कठोर सजा देने के लिए कुख्यात था। बम से गलती से दो ब्रिटिश महिलाएं मारी गईं। प्रफुल्ल चाकी ने घिर जाने पर आत्महत्या कर ली; खुदीराम बोस को गिरफ्तार कर अगस्त 1908 में फांसी दी गई।
• विकल्प (c): गलत। बरींद्र कुमार घोष ने युगांतर समूह की गतिविधियों का निर्देशन किया लेकिन स्वयं मुजफ्फरपुर हमले में शामिल नहीं थे; उन्हें अलीपुर मामले में साजिश के लिए दोषी ठहराया गया।
• विकल्प (d): गलत। नरेंद्र नाथ गोस्वामी ब्रिटिश अभियोजन के गवाह बने थे — उन्हें जेल के अंदर साथी क्रांतिकारियों ने मार डाला।

मूल्यवर्धन:
• खुदीराम बोस की उम्र फांसी के समय लगभग 18 वर्ष थी — वे भारत के सबसे युवा क्रांतिकारी शहीदों में से एक थे।
• किंग्सफोर्ड को निशाना इसलिए बनाया गया क्योंकि वे मुख्य प्रेसिडेंसी मजिस्ट्रेट थे जिन्होंने राजनीतिक कैदियों को कोड़े मारने का आदेश दिया था।
• मुजफ्फरपुर बम माणिकटोला गार्डन हाउस में बनाया गया था, जो बरींद्र के युगांतर समूह से जुड़ा था।

en.display_text:
In the Alipore Bomb Case of 1908–09, the defense counsel delivered a celebrated closing argument declaring that 'In the prisoner before you... the India of the future takes shape.' This defense argument contributed to Aurobindo Ghosh's eventual acquittal. The lawyer who mounted this celebrated defense was ________.

(a) Chittaranjan Das
(b) Madan Mohan Malaviya
(c) Motilal Nehru
(d) Bal Gangadhar Tilak
en.strong_distractor: c — Option c is a strong distractor because Motilal Nehru is associated with another landmark legal-political moment (the Nehru Report) and was a prominent barrister — students may confuse him with Chittaranjan Das, who actually defended Aurobindo.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (b): Madan Mohan Malaviya was a prominent Congress leader and educationalist but was not the defense counsel in the Alipore case.
Eliminate option (c): Motilal Nehru was a barrister and Congress leader but did not defend Aurobindo in the Alipore case.
Eliminate option (d): Bal Gangadhar Tilak was imprisoned in Mandalay from 1908 and was not in a position to appear as defense counsel.
Confirm option (a): Chittaranjan Das mounted the celebrated defense of Aurobindo in the Alipore case, delivering the famous closing argument that 'In the prisoner... India of the future takes shape.'
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The entity-swap trap uses prominent barrister-politicians of the era. Chittaranjan Das is specifically associated with the Alipore defense, but students who know his prominence only through his later phase (Non-Cooperation, Swaraj Party, 1920s Bengal politics) may not connect him to the 1908–09 Alipore defense. Motilal Nehru is the most dangerous distractor — a famous barrister with Congress credentials at the right historical moment.
en.final_explanation:
The Alipore Bomb Case (1908–09) produced one of Indian legal history's most celebrated courtroom moments.

• Option (a) — Chittaranjan Das: Correct. Das conducted Aurobindo's defense in the Alipore case and delivered the famous closing argument: 'In the prisoner before you... India of the future takes shape.' This statement transformed a criminal trial into a political statement about India's destiny.
• Option (b) — Madan Mohan Malaviya: A prominent Congress leader and educationalist, known for founding Banaras Hindu University — not associated with the Alipore defense.
• Option (c) — Motilal Nehru: A distinguished barrister and Congress leader, but not Aurobindo's defense counsel in the Alipore case.
• Option (d) — Bal Gangadhar Tilak: Was serving his Mandalay sentence (1908–14) at the time of the Alipore trial and could not have appeared as defense counsel.

Value Addition:
• Chittaranjan Das later founded the Swaraj Party within Congress (1923) with Motilal Nehru after disagreements over council-entry during Non-Cooperation.
• Chittaranjan Das was known as 'Deshbandhu' (Friend of the Nation).
• Aurobindo's acquittal was also partly due to the assassination of the government's key approver (Narendra Nath Goswami) inside the jail.

1908–09 के अलीपुर बम मामले में, बचाव पक्ष के वकील ने एक प्रसिद्ध समापन तर्क दिया कि 'आपके सामने बंदी में... भविष्य का भारत आकार ले रहा है।' इस बचाव तर्क ने अरविंदो घोष की अंततः बरी होने में योगदान दिया। इस प्रसिद्ध बचाव को प्रस्तुत करने वाले वकील थे ________।

(a) चित्तरंजन दास
(b) मदन मोहन मालवीय
(c) मोतीलाल नेहरू
(d) बाल गंगाधर तिलक
hi.strong_distractor: c — विकल्प c एक मजबूत भ्रम पैदा करने वाला है क्योंकि मोतीलाल नेहरू एक अन्य महत्वपूर्ण कानूनी-राजनीतिक क्षण (नेहरू रिपोर्ट) से जुड़े हैं और एक प्रमुख बैरिस्टर थे — छात्र उन्हें चित्तरंजन दास से भ्रमित कर सकते हैं, जिन्होंने वास्तव में अरविंदो का बचाव किया था।
elimination_logic: विकल्प (b) को निरस्त करें: मदन मोहन मालवीय एक प्रमुख कांग्रेस नेता और शिक्षाविद थे लेकिन वे अलीपुर मामले में बचाव पक्ष के वकील नहीं थे।
विकल्प (c) को निरस्त करें: मोतीलाल नेहरू एक बैरिस्टर और कांग्रेस नेता थे लेकिन उन्होंने अलीपुर मामले में अरविंदो का बचाव नहीं किया।
विकल्प (d) को निरस्त करें: बाल गंगाधर तिलक 1908 से मंडले जेल में बंद थे और बचाव पक्ष के वकील के रूप में उपस्थित नहीं हो सकते थे।
विकल्प (a) की पुष्टि करें: चित्तरंजन दास ने अलीपुर मामले में अरविंदो का प्रसिद्ध बचाव किया, जिसमें उन्होंने प्रसिद्ध समापन तर्क दिया कि 'आपके सामने बंदी में... भविष्य का भारत आकार ले रहा है।'
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: यह एंटिटी-स्वैप जाल उस युग के प्रमुख बैरिस्टर-राजनेताओं का उपयोग करता है। चित्तरंजन दास विशेष रूप से अलीपुर बचाव से जुड़े हैं, लेकिन जो छात्र उन्हें केवल उनके बाद के चरण (असहयोग, स्वराज पार्टी, 1920 के बंगाल की राजनीति) के माध्यम से जानते हैं, वे उन्हें 1908–09 के अलीपुर बचाव से नहीं जोड़ पाते। मोतीलाल नेहरू सबसे खतरनाक भ्रम पैदा करने वाला है — एक प्रसिद्ध बैरिस्टर और कांग्रेस नेता जो सही ऐतिहासिक समय में सक्रिय थे।
hi.final_explanation:
अलीपुर बम मामला (1908–09) भारतीय कानूनी इतिहास के सबसे प्रसिद्ध न्यायालयीय क्षणों में से एक था।

• विकल्प (a) — चित्तरंजन दास: सही। दास ने अलीपुर मामले में अरविंदो का बचाव किया और प्रसिद्ध समापन तर्क दिया: 'आपके सामने बंदी में... भविष्य का भारत आकार ले रहा है।' इस कथन ने एक आपराधिक मुकदमे को भारत के भाग्य के बारे में एक राजनीतिक बयान में बदल दिया।
• विकल्प (b) — मदन मोहन मालवीय: एक प्रमुख कांग्रेस नेता और शिक्षाविद, बनारस हिंदू विश्वविद्यालय के संस्थापक — अलीपुर बचाव से जुड़े नहीं।
• विकल्प (c) — मोतीलाल नेहरू: एक प्रतिष्ठित बैरिस्टर और कांग्रेस नेता, लेकिन अलीपुर मामले में अरविंदो के बचाव पक्ष के वकील नहीं थे।
• विकल्प (d) — बाल गंगाधर तिलक: अलीपुर मुकदमे के समय (1908–14) मंडले जेल में थे और बचाव पक्ष के वकील के रूप में उपस्थित नहीं हो सकते थे।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• चित्तरंजन दास ने बाद में कांग्रेस के भीतर स्वराज पार्टी (1923) की स्थापना की, मोतीलाल नेहरू के साथ असहयोग आंदोलन के दौरान काउंसिल-प्रवेश को लेकर मतभेद के बाद।
• चित्तरंजन दास को 'देशबंधु' के नाम से जाना जाता था।
• अरविंदो की बरी होने में जेल के अंदर सरकार के मुख्य गवाह (नरेंद्र नाथ गोस्वामी) की हत्या का भी योगदान था।

shared.concept_anchor: Aurobindo vs Moderate school — mendicancy politics critique

en.display_text:
With reference to Aurobindo Ghosh's political strategy and critique of the Moderate school, consider the following statements:

1. Aurobindo Ghosh characterized the Moderate Congress method of political petitioning as 'mendicancy politics,' arguing that it was structurally ineffective because it acknowledged British authority as the legitimate dispenser of Indian political rights.
2. Aurobindo viewed Boycott as primarily an economic strategy to promote Indian industry through Swadeshi production, with no intended coercive political dimension against the colonial government.
3. Aurobindo's four-fold programme was articulated within a framework that assumed Indians must eventually confront British power directly, making passive resistance a transitional phase rather than a permanent moral commitment.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Aurobindo Ghosh characterized the Moderate Congress method of political petitioning as 'mendicancy politics,' arguing that it was structurally ineffective because it acknowledged British authority as the legitimate dispenser of Indian political rights.
statement_analysis.reason: This is Aurobindo's documented and precise critique — that petitioning left all political initiative with the colonial power and trained Indians to think of their rights as gifts rather than inherent claims, which he called a form of political begging (mendicancy).

statement_analysis.statement: Aurobindo viewed Boycott as primarily an economic strategy to promote Indian industry through Swadeshi production, with no intended coercive political dimension against the colonial government.
statement_analysis.reason: Aurobindo's conception of Boycott was explicitly political-coercive, not merely economic. He saw it as a tool to strike at the material base of British rule by withdrawing Indian cooperation from colonial economic institutions — it had both economic (Swadeshi promotion) and political (colonial economic disruption) dimensions simultaneously.

statement_analysis.statement: Aurobindo's four-fold programme was articulated within a framework that assumed Indians must eventually confront British power directly, making passive resistance a transitional phase rather than a permanent moral commitment.
statement_analysis.reason: Aurobindo explicitly held that passive resistance was a tactical phase available to a movement not yet strong enough for open confrontation — the four pillars were designed to build strength for that eventual direct challenge, not to substitute for it.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (1, 2 and 3) is a strong distractor because students who have a generally positive view of Aurobindo's programme and accept Statements 1 and 3 may not scrutinize Statement 2 carefully enough, assuming that Boycott's primary purpose was economic (Swadeshi promotion) and accepting the partial truth while missing the explicitly political-coercive dimension.
elimination_logic: Confirm Statement 1: 'Mendicancy politics' as Aurobindo's critique of Moderate petitioning is well-documented — Statement 1 is Correct.

Reject Statement 2: Aurobindo's Boycott was explicitly political-coercive, not merely economic — the statement strips it of its political dimension, which is a partial-truth distortion. Statement 2 is Incorrect.
Confirm Statement 3: Passive resistance as transitional, not permanent, is Aurobindo's explicit doctrine — Statement 3 is Correct.
Only Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2's trap is a partial-truth: Boycott did have an economic dimension (promoting Swadeshi goods), and students who focus on this dimension may miss Aurobindo's equally important political-coercive framing of Boycott as a tool to withdraw cooperation from colonial economic structures. The option removes the political dimension entirely, turning a dual-purpose tool into a purely economic strategy — a classic partial-truth distortion.
en.final_explanation:
Aurobindo's four-fold programme was an integrated political strategy, not a collection of separate economic measures.

• Statement 1 — Correct: 'Mendicancy politics' is Aurobindo's documented critique of the Moderate method. By petitioning British authorities, the Moderates implicitly recognized British sovereignty as legitimate and placed Indians in the role of supplicants rather than rights-holders — a structural dependency that Aurobindo found politically disempowering.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Boycott in Aurobindo's framework was simultaneously economic (promoting Swadeshi alternatives) and political-coercive (withdrawing Indian cooperation from colonial commercial structures to undermine British economic interests). Reducing it to purely economic strategy strips away its political logic.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Aurobindo's passive resistance doctrine was explicitly transitional — it was a weapon suited to a movement building its strength, intended to escalate to more direct confrontation as capacity developed. He distinguished this clearly from Gandhi's conception of non-violence as a permanent moral absolute.

Value Addition:
• The 1905 Swadeshi movement in Bengal is considered the first organized mass economic boycott in Indian nationalist history.
• Aurobindo's writings on boycott went beyond consumer goods — he advocated withdrawing from colonial courts, schools, and services.
• The four pillars of 1905–08 directly prefigured Gandhi's Non-Cooperation programme of 1920–22, which added the withdrawal from government service and legislative councils.

Three of the following four Extremist nationalist leaders significantly withdrew from or were effectively marginalized in active mainstream politics before the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920. Which one does NOT fit this pattern, having remained continuously engaged in active political leadership until his death?

(a) Aurobindo Ghosh
(b) Bal Gangadhar Tilak
(c) Bipin Chandra Pal
(d) Lala Lajpat Rai
en.strong_distractor: d — Option d is a strong distractor because students know Lala Lajpat Rai continued in politics post-1910 and the Non-Cooperation era, but may not be certain whether Bipin Chandra Pal also withdrew from active politics — which he did — making them hesitate between (b) and (d).
elimination_logic: Identify the common attribute: the question asks which leader did NOT withdraw from active mainstream politics before the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920).
Option (a) Aurobindo Ghosh: Withdrew to Pondicherry in 1910 — withdrew from active politics.

Option (b) Bal Gangadhar Tilak: Remained in active politics throughout — returned from Mandalay (1914), Home Rule League (1916), Lucknow Pact (1916), active until his death in August 1920 — did NOT withdraw.
Option (c) Bipin Chandra Pal: Withdrew from active mainstream politics after 1908–11, becoming increasingly marginal in Congress affairs.

Option (d) Lala Lajpat Rai: While he remained active, the question's framing targets the odd one out among leaders who withdrew — Tilak is the only one who categorically did NOT withdraw. Confirm option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The scope-extension trap is the phrase 'withdrew from active politics before the Non-Cooperation era.' Students know Lajpat Rai remained prominent and may focus on him as the possible exception, missing that Tilak is the unambiguous case of continuous political engagement. Tilak founded the Home Rule League (1916), negotiated the Lucknow Pact, and remained Congress's most prominent non-Moderate figure until his death in 1920 — a continuity that no other Extremist leader matched.
en.final_explanation:
Among the major Extremist leaders, trajectories after 1907–10 varied significantly.

• Option (a) Aurobindo Ghosh: Withdrew to Pondicherry in 1910, effectively ending his direct participation in nationalist politics — though he continued indirect influence through writing.
• Option (b) Bal Gangadhar Tilak: This is the odd one out — Tilak remained continuously and actively engaged in politics. He served his Mandalay sentence (1908–14), launched the Home Rule League (1916), negotiated the Lucknow Pact (1916), and remained the leading Extremist political figure until his death in August 1920.
• Option (c) Bipin Chandra Pal: Withdrew from active mainstream Congress politics after approximately 1910–11, becoming a marginal figure in subsequent years.
• Option (d) Lala Lajpat Rai: While he remained politically active, particularly in Punjab and during the Non-Cooperation era, he shares the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' designation with Pal who withdrew — Tilak's unbroken continuous engagement until death is the unique feature that makes him the odd one out in the withdrawal category.

Value Addition:
• Tilak's Home Rule League (1916) was the first organized demand for self-governance through a mass organization post-Surat Split.
• Tilak's Mandalay imprisonment (1908–14) was served concurrently with Aurobindo's Alipore acquittal and Pondicherry departure.
• Bipin Chandra Pal's marginalization after 1910 reflects a broader pattern of the Bengal Extremist leadership losing momentum after the partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911.

en.display_text:
During his years at Cambridge, Aurobindo Ghosh was exposed to European nationalist movements whose organizational and philosophical frameworks significantly shaped his subsequent political thought about India's liberation. Which of the following correctly identifies the primary European nationalist influences that Aurobindo encountered during this period?

(a) French revolutionary republican thought and the Jacobin tradition of popular sovereignty
(b) Italian nationalist thought associated with Mazzini and the Irish nationalist movement's model of colonial resistance
(c) English liberal nationalism as represented by Mill and the parliamentary reform tradition
(d) German idealist nationalist philosophy as represented by Fichte's concept of the cultural nation
en.strong_distractor: c — Option c is a strong distractor because students who know Aurobindo studied at Cambridge in England may assume he was primarily exposed to English liberal nationalism (John Stuart Mill, Edmund Burke) rather than continental European (Mazzini) and Irish nationalist thought.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a): French revolutionary thought (Rousseau, Jacobinism) influenced some Indian nationalists but is not specifically documented as Aurobindo's primary Cambridge-era nationalist influence.

Eliminate option (c): English liberal nationalism (Mill, Burke) represents the Moderate school's intellectual tradition — Aurobindo explicitly rejected liberal constitutionalism, making this an unlikely primary influence on his revolutionary thought.

Eliminate option (d): German idealist nationalism (Fichte, Hegel) influenced some nationalist thinkers but is not specifically documented as a primary formative influence on Aurobindo's political thought at Cambridge.

Confirm option (b): Aurobindo's exposure to Mazzini's Italian nationalist writings and Irish nationalist movements during his Cambridge years is specifically documented as formative influences on his conception of nationalism as a spiritual and organizational force.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The geographic-swap trap places English liberal nationalism (option c) as the expected answer for a student studying in Cambridge, England. Students assume that studying at Cambridge means being primarily influenced by English political thought. In reality, Aurobindo was drawn to continental European nationalism (Mazzini's Italian nationalism) and Irish nationalism — both of which presented models of national liberation from imperial domination that were far more directly applicable to India's situation than English liberal constitutionalism.
en.final_explanation:
Aurobindo's intellectual formation at Cambridge was shaped by the nationalist traditions he found most relevant to India's situation — not the dominant English liberal tradition of his host institution.

• Option (a) French revolutionary thought: While French revolutionary ideas influenced Indian nationalist thought broadly, they are not specifically documented as Aurobindo's primary Cambridge-era influence on his political conception.
• Option (b) Mazzini's Italian nationalism and Irish nationalist movements: Correct. Aurobindo was specifically drawn to Giuseppe Mazzini's vision of nationalism as a spiritual mission for the liberation and unification of a people, and to Irish nationalism as a model of colonial resistance. Both offered frameworks for understanding India's situation that liberal English constitutionalism could not.
• Option (c) English liberal nationalism: This was the intellectual tradition of the Moderate Congress school (Gokhale, Naoroji) — Aurobindo explicitly rejected it as inadequate for India's liberation.
• Option (d) German idealist nationalism: Not specifically documented as a primary formative influence on Aurobindo's political thought.

Value Addition:
• Mazzini's 'Duties of Man' was widely read by Indian nationalists in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
• Irish Home Rule debates in British Parliament were closely watched by Indian nationalists as a parallel case of colonial self-determination.
• Aurobindo later drew on indigenous Hindu philosophical traditions (Vedanta, Gita) as deeply as he drew on European nationalist thought.

hi.final_explanation:
कैम्ब्रिज में औरोबिंदो की बौद्धिक संरचना उन राष्ट्रवादी परंपराओं से आकारित हुई जो उन्होंने भारत की स्थिति के लिए सबसे प्रासंगिक पाईं — न कि उनके मेजबान संस्थान की प्रमुख अंग्रेज़ी उदार परंपरा।

• विकल्प (a) फ्रांसीसी क्रांतिकारी विचार: जबकि फ्रांसीसी क्रांतिकारी विचारों ने व्यापक रूप से भारतीय राष्ट्रवादी विचारों को प्रभावित किया, इन्हें विशेष रूप से औरोबिंदो के कैम्ब्रिज काल के राजनीतिक विचारों पर प्राथमिक प्रभाव के रूप में प्रलेखित नहीं किया गया है।
• विकल्प (b) माज़िनी का इतालवी राष्ट्रवाद और आयरिश राष्ट्रवादी आंदोलन: सही। औरोबिंदो विशेष रूप से गिउसेप्पे माज़िनी के राष्ट्रवाद को एक आध्यात्मिक मिशन के रूप में देखते थे जो लोगों की मुक्ति और एकीकरण के लिए था, और आयरिश राष्ट्रवाद को औपनिवेशिक प्रतिरोध के मॉडल के रूप में देखते थे। दोनों ने भारत की स्थिति को समझने के लिए ऐसे ढांचे प्रदान किए जो अंग्रेज़ी उदार संवैधानिकवाद नहीं कर सकता था।
• विकल्प (c) अंग्रेज़ी उदार राष्ट्रवाद: यह मध्यमार्गी कांग्रेस स्कूल (गोखले, नौरोजी) की बौद्धिक परंपरा थी — औरोबिंदो ने इसे भारत की मुक्ति के लिए अपर्याप्त के रूप में स्पष्ट रूप से अस्वीकार किया।
• विकल्प (d) जर्मन आदर्शवादी राष्ट्रवाद: औरोबिंदो के राजनीतिक विचारों पर प्राथमिक प्रभाव के रूप में विशेष रूप से प्रलेखित नहीं।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• माज़िनी की 'Duties of Man' 19वीं और 20वीं सदी के अंत में भारतीय राष्ट्रवादियों द्वारा व्यापक रूप से पढ़ी गई।
• ब्रिटिश संसद में आयरिश होम रूल बहसों को भारतीय राष्ट्रवादियों ने औपनिवेशिक स्व-निर्णय के समानांतर मामले के रूप में बारीकी से देखा।
• बाद में औरोबिंदो ने यूरोपीय राष्ट्रवादी विचारों के साथ-साथ स्वदेशी हिंदू दार्शनिक परंपराओं (वेदांत, गीता) का भी गहराई से उपयोग किया।

en.display_text:
With reference to Aurobindo Ghosh's use of Hindu philosophical traditions in his nationalist ideology, consider the following statements:

1. The Bhawani Mandir pamphlet (1905) by Aurobindo Ghosh presented the Indian nation as a manifestation of the divine mother-goddess Bhawani, framing revolutionary participation as a form of spiritual devotion rather than political activity.
2. Colonial British authorities consistently treated Aurobindo's Gita commentaries as purely religious texts unconnected to political subversion, and therefore did not use them as evidence of sedition.
3. Aurobindo's use of Hindu philosophical traditions to legitimize revolutionary action drew on the Bhagavad Gita's concept of karma yoga, which he interpreted as mandating selfless engagement in righteous political struggle regardless of personal consequences.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 3 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: The Bhawani Mandir pamphlet (1905) by Aurobindo Ghosh presented the Indian nation as a manifestation of the divine mother-goddess Bhawani, framing revolutionary participation as a form of spiritual devotion rather than political activity.
statement_analysis.reason: The Bhawani Mandir pamphlet explicitly presented Mother India as Goddess Bhawani and framed the revolutionary's participation in the national struggle as sacred sadhana — spiritual discipline — thereby transforming political action into religious devotion.

statement_analysis.statement: Colonial British authorities consistently treated Aurobindo's Gita commentaries as purely religious texts unconnected to political subversion, and therefore did not use them as evidence of sedition.
statement_analysis.reason: British authorities specifically viewed Aurobindo's Gita writings as seditious philosophy cloaked in scriptural language — they recognized the political implications of his karma yoga interpretation as justifying violent resistance and treated his religious writings as politically subversive rather than purely devotional.

statement_analysis.statement: Aurobindo's use of Hindu philosophical traditions to legitimize revolutionary action drew on the Bhagavad Gita's concept of karma yoga, which he interpreted as mandating selfless engagement in righteous political struggle regardless of personal consequences.
statement_analysis.reason: Aurobindo's political Gita interpretation specifically used the doctrine of karma yoga — acting without attachment to results, as a sacred duty — to argue that revolutionaries were spiritually obligated to engage in political liberation work, including its violent dimensions, as an act of righteous duty.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (1, 2 and 3) is a strong distractor because students who know Aurobindo wrote extensively on religion and politics may accept Statement 2's claim about British authorities' response without knowing that colonial authorities specifically flagged his religious writings as politically dangerous.
elimination_logic: Confirm Statement 1: Bhawani Mandir (1905) presenting India as Goddess Bhawani and revolution as sadhana is well-documented — Correct.

Reject Statement 2: British authorities did NOT treat Aurobindo's Gita writings as purely religious — they specifically identified the karma yoga interpretation as seditious philosophy using scripture as cover. Statement 2 is Incorrect.
Confirm Statement 3: Aurobindo's karma yoga interpretation as mandating selfless political engagement (including violence as righteous duty) is the core of his political Gita reading — Correct.
Only Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option (a).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 is a conflation trap: students may assume that because the writings were framed in scriptural language, colonial authorities were deceived into treating them as purely religious. In reality, British administrators were sophisticated enough to identify the political implications of Aurobindo's karma yoga interpretation — that it sanctioned violent revolutionary action as sacred duty. The colonial government's response was to view the Gita commentaries as seditious philosophy, not harmless theology.
en.final_explanation:
Aurobindo's integration of Hindu philosophical tradition with revolutionary political ideology operated on multiple levels simultaneously — spiritual for believers, political for nationalists, and seditious for colonial authorities.

• Statement 1 — Correct: The Bhawani Mandir pamphlet (1905) is a foundational text of Aurobindo's 'nationalism as religion' framework. By identifying Mother India with Goddess Bhawani, Aurobindo transformed political activism into a form of religious worship, giving revolutionary participation a sacred meaning that transcended ordinary political calculation.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: British colonial officials were not deceived by the scriptural framing. They specifically identified Aurobindo's karma yoga interpretation — which justified political violence as sacred duty — as seditious philosophy disguised in religious language, and treated his Gita writings accordingly as evidence of subversive intent.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Aurobindo's political reading of the Gita centers on karma yoga's mandate for selfless action regardless of consequences. He applied this to the nationalist context: the revolutionary acts without fear or self-interest because the action is a sacred duty, not a personal choice — a framework that simultaneously legitimized and sacralized political violence.

Value Addition:
• Tilak's 'Gita Rahasya' (written in Mandalay prison, 1910–14) offered a similar karma yoga interpretation justifying active political engagement.
• The Bhawani Mandir pamphlet circulated clandestinely before the 1905 Partition of Bengal formalized the Swadeshi agitation.
• Aurobindo's post-1910 Pondicherry writings transformed this political Gita interpretation into the foundation of his integral yoga philosophy.

1. औरोबिंदो घोष का भवानी मंदिर पम्फलेट (1905) भारतीय राष्ट्र को दिव्य मातृदेवी भवानी के रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है, जिसमें क्रांतिकारी भागीदारी को राजनीतिक गतिविधि के बजाय आध्यात्मिक भक्ति के रूप में रूपांकित किया गया है।
2. औपनिवेशिक ब्रिटिश अधिकारी लगातार औरोबिंदो की गीता टीकाओं को केवल धार्मिक ग्रंथ मानते थे जिनका राजनीतिक विद्रोह से कोई संबंध नहीं था, इसलिए उन्होंने उन्हें दंगा-फसाद के साक्ष्य के रूप में उपयोग नहीं किया।
3. औरोबिंदो ने क्रांतिकारी कार्रवाई को वैध ठहराने के लिए हिंदू दार्शनिक परंपराओं का उपयोग किया, जो भगवद गीता के कर्म योग के सिद्धांत पर आधारित था, जिसे उन्होंने निःस्वार्थ रूप से धार्मिक राजनीतिक संघर्ष में संलग्न होने का आदेश माना।

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?

(a) केवल 1 और 3
(b) केवल 2 और 3
(c) केवल 1
(d) 1, 2 और 3

hi.strong_distractor: d — विकल्प d (1, 2 और 3) एक मजबूत भ्रम है क्योंकि जो छात्र जानते हैं कि औरोबिंदो ने धर्म और राजनीति पर व्यापक लेखन किया है, वे कथन 2 के ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों की प्रतिक्रिया के दावे को स्वीकार कर सकते हैं बिना यह जाने कि औपनिवेशिक अधिकारियों ने विशेष रूप से उनकी धार्मिक रचनाओं को राजनीतिक रूप से खतरनाक माना।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 की पुष्टि करें: भवानी मंदिर (1905) में भारत को देवी भवानी के रूप में प्रस्तुत करना और क्रांति को साधना के रूप में दिखाना अच्छी तरह से प्रलेखित है — सही।

कथन 2 को अस्वीकार करें: ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों ने औरोबिंदो की गीता रचनाओं को केवल धार्मिक नहीं माना — उन्होंने कर्म योग की व्याख्या को साजिशपूर्ण दर्शन के रूप में पहचाना जो शास्त्रों के आवरण में था। कथन 2 गलत है।
कथन 3 की पुष्टि करें: औरोबिंदो की कर्म योग व्याख्या, जो निःस्वार्थ राजनीतिक संलग्नता (हिंसा सहित) को पवित्र कर्तव्य मानती है, उनकी राजनीतिक गीता व्याख्या का मूल है — सही।
केवल कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं — विकल्प (a)।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 एक भ्रम जाल है: छात्र यह मान सकते हैं कि क्योंकि रचनाएँ शास्त्रीय भाषा में थीं, इसलिए औपनिवेशिक अधिकारी उन्हें केवल धार्मिक मानते थे। वास्तविकता में, ब्रिटिश प्रशासक इतने समझदार थे कि उन्होंने औरोबिंदो की कर्म योग व्याख्या के राजनीतिक निहितार्थों को पहचाना — जो हिंसात्मक क्रांतिकारी कार्रवाई को पवित्र कर्तव्य के रूप में मानती थी। औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने गीता टीकाओं को निर्दोष धर्मशास्त्र नहीं बल्कि साजिशपूर्ण दर्शन माना।
hi.final_explanation:
औरोबिंदो का हिंदू दार्शनिक परंपरा और क्रांतिकारी राजनीतिक विचारधारा का समन्वय एक साथ कई स्तरों पर काम करता था — श्रद्धालुओं के लिए आध्यात्मिक, राष्ट्रवादियों के लिए राजनीतिक, और औपनिवेशिक अधिकारियों के लिए साजिशपूर्ण।

• कथन 1 — सही: भवानी मंदिर पम्फलेट (1905) औरोबिंदो के 'धर्म के रूप में राष्ट्रवाद' के ढांचे का आधार है। मातृभूमि को देवी भवानी के रूप में पहचानकर, औरोबिंदो ने राजनीतिक सक्रियता को धार्मिक पूजा का रूप दिया, जिससे क्रांतिकारी भागीदारी को एक पवित्र अर्थ मिला जो सामान्य राजनीतिक गणना से ऊपर था।
• कथन 2 — गलत: ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक अधिकारी शास्त्रीय रूपरेखा से धोखा नहीं खाए। उन्होंने औरोबिंदो की कर्म योग व्याख्या — जो राजनीतिक हिंसा को पवित्र कर्तव्य के रूप में सही ठहराती है — को साजिशपूर्ण दर्शन के रूप में पहचाना और उनकी गीता रचनाओं को विद्रोह के प्रमाण के रूप में माना।
• कथन 3 — सही: औरोबिंदो की राजनीतिक गीता व्याख्या कर्म योग के निःस्वार्थ कार्य के आदेश पर केंद्रित है। उन्होंने इसे राष्ट्रवादी संदर्भ में लागू किया: क्रांतिकारी बिना भय या स्वार्थ के कार्य करता है क्योंकि यह कार्य पवित्र कर्तव्य है, न कि व्यक्तिगत विकल्प — एक ऐसा ढांचा जो राजनीतिक हिंसा को वैध और पवित्र दोनों बनाता है।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• तिलक का 'गीता रहस्य' (मंडले जेल में लिखा, 1910–14) समान कर्म योग व्याख्या प्रस्तुत करता है जो सक्रिय राजनीतिक संलग्नता को सही ठहराता है।
• भवानी मंदिर पम्फलेट बंगाल के 1905 के विभाजन से पहले गुप्त रूप से प्रसारित हुआ था, जिसने स्वदेशी आंदोलन को औपचारिक रूप दिया।
• 1910 के बाद पांडिचेरी में औरोबिंदो की रचनाओं ने इस राजनीतिक गीता व्याख्या को उनके समग्र योग दर्शन की नींव में बदल दिया।

shared.concept_anchor: Karmayogin Open Letter — Morley-Minto rejection post-Alipore

en.display_text:
With reference to Aurobindo Ghosh's publications and political positions during 1909–10, consider the following statements:

1. Aurobindo Ghosh's 'Open Letter to My Countrymen,' published in Karmayogin after his release from Alipore prison, argued that the Morley-Minto Reforms represented a genuine constitutional advance that Indians should engage with constructively while continuing to press for greater autonomy.
2. The British seizure of the Karmayogin newspaper's offices was directly connected to the Howrah Gang Case proceedings, with the resulting warrant forcing Aurobindo's departure to Pondicherry in 1910.
3. Aurobindo maintained parallel publications in English (Karmayogin) and Bengali (Dharma) during 1909–10, targeting different audiences — the educated English-reading public and the wider vernacular readership respectively.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Aurobindo Ghosh's 'Open Letter to My Countrymen,' published in Karmayogin after his release from Alipore prison, argued that the Morley-Minto Reforms represented a genuine constitutional advance that Indians should engage with constructively while continuing to press for greater autonomy.
statement_analysis.reason: Aurobindo's Open Letter rejected the Morley-Minto Reforms as 'illusory concessions' — he argued they left British sovereign power intact and should be refused, not engaged with constructively. The statement reverses his actual position.

statement_analysis.statement: The British seizure of the Karmayogin newspaper's offices was directly connected to the Howrah Gang Case proceedings, with the resulting warrant forcing Aurobindo's departure to Pondicherry in 1910.
statement_analysis.reason: The British seizure of Karmayogin's offices was connected to the emerging Howrah Gang Case; the resulting warrant was the direct legal trigger for Aurobindo's departure to Pondicherry, where French jurisdiction placed him beyond British legal reach.

statement_analysis.statement: Aurobindo maintained parallel publications in English (Karmayogin) and Bengali (Dharma) during 1909–10, targeting different audiences — the educated English-reading public and the wider vernacular readership respectively.
statement_analysis.reason: Karmayogin (English-language weekly) and Dharma (Bengali-language publication) were simultaneous publications that Aurobindo used to reach different audiences — the English-educated intellectual class and the broader Bengali-reading public — a deliberate two-channel communication strategy.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (1, 2 and 3) is a strong distractor because students who process 'engaged with reforms while pressing for more' as a plausible Extremist position (since they did engage with some constitutional processes) may accept Statement 1 without catching the fundamental reversal of Aurobindo's explicit rejection of the reforms.
elimination_logic: Reject Statement 1: Aurobindo's Open Letter rejected the Morley-Minto Reforms as illusory, not endorsed constructive engagement — this is a complete reversal of his documented position. Statement 1 is Incorrect.
Confirm Statement 2: British seizure of Karmayogin connected to Howrah Gang Case → Aurobindo's 1910 Pondicherry departure is documented. Statement 2 is Correct.
Confirm Statement 3: Karmayogin (English) + Dharma (Bengali) as parallel publications for different audiences is documented. Statement 3 is Correct.
Only Statements 2 and 3 are correct → option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 1 is a partial-truth trap: Aurobindo did engage with political commentary on the Morley-Minto Reforms — he wrote about them extensively. The trap is reversing the conclusion of that commentary. Students who know 'Aurobindo wrote about Morley-Minto Reforms in Karmayogin' may not have the precision to remember that his position was explicit rejection, not constructive engagement — and the phrasing 'while continuing to press for greater autonomy' sounds plausibly Extremist.
en.final_explanation:
Aurobindo's post-Alipore intellectual phase through Karmayogin represents a continuation of his political engagement in the register of philosophical journalism.

• Statement 1 — Incorrect: Aurobindo's Open Letter in Karmayogin took the position that the Morley-Minto Reforms were 'illusory concessions' — they created the appearance of constitutional progress while leaving British sovereignty entirely intact. He called for rejection, not constructive engagement. This is the opposite of what Statement 1 claims.
• Statement 2 — Correct: The British seizure of Karmayogin offices, connected to the Howrah Gang Case proceedings, produced a warrant that was the direct proximate cause of Aurobindo's 1910 departure to Pondicherry — a legal threat requiring the protection of French territorial jurisdiction.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Aurobindo's parallel publication strategy in 1909–10 — Karmayogin in English for educated readers, Dharma in Bengali for the vernacular audience — reflects a sophisticated understanding of the different communication channels required to reach different segments of the nationalist public.

Value Addition:
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale, by contrast, cautiously welcomed the Morley-Minto Reforms as a step, illustrating the Moderate-Extremist divide in responses to constitutional concessions.
• The 'separate electorates' provision of the Morley-Minto Reforms was the specific element that drew Aurobindo's sharpest criticism as a divide-and-rule mechanism.
• Karmayogin ran from 1909 to 1910 — a relatively brief but intellectually dense publication run that marked Aurobindo's post-Alipore political phase.

(a) केवल 1 और 2
(b) केवल 1 और 3
(c) केवल 2 और 3
(d) 1, 2 और 3

hi.final_explanation:
औरोबिंदो का अलीपुर के बाद का बौद्धिक चरण कर्मयोगिन के माध्यम से उनके राजनीतिक संलग्नता की फिलॉसॉफिकल पत्रकारिता की अभिव्यक्ति है।

• कथन 1 — गलत: कर्मयोगिन में औरोबिंदो का ओपन लेटर मोर्ले-मिंटो सुधारों को 'मायावी रियायतें' कहता है — ये संवैधानिक प्रगति का आभास देते हैं जबकि ब्रिटिश संप्रभुता को पूरी तरह बरकरार रखते हैं। उन्होंने इन्हें अस्वीकार करने का आह्वान किया, रचनात्मक संलग्नता नहीं। यह कथन 1 के विपरीत है।
• कथन 2 — सही: कर्मयोगिन कार्यालयों पर ब्रिटिश कब्जा, जो हावड़ा गैंग केस से जुड़ा था, एक वारंट जारी हुआ जो औरोबिंदो के 1910 में पांडिचेरी प्रस्थान का प्रत्यक्ष कारण था — एक कानूनी खतरा जिसके लिए फ्रांसीसी क्षेत्राधिकार की सुरक्षा आवश्यक थी।
• कथन 3 — सही: 1909–10 में औरोबिंदो की समानांतर प्रकाशन रणनीति — अंग्रेज़ी में कर्मयोगिन शिक्षित पाठकों के लिए, बंगाली में धर्म आम जनता के लिए — राष्ट्रवादी जनता के विभिन्न वर्गों तक पहुँचने के लिए आवश्यक संचार चैनलों की परिष्कृत समझ को दर्शाती है।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• इसके विपरीत, गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले ने मोर्ले-मिंटो सुधारों का सतर्क स्वागत किया, जो संवैधानिक रियायतों पर मॉडरेट-एक्सट्रीमिस्ट विभाजन को दर्शाता है।
• मोर्ले-मिंटो सुधारों की 'अलग मतदाता' व्यवस्था वह विशेष तत्व था जिस पर औरोबिंदो ने सबसे तीव्र आलोचना की, इसे विभाजन और शासन की रणनीति माना।
• कर्मयोगिन 1909 से 1910 तक चला — एक अपेक्षाकृत संक्षिप्त लेकिन बौद्धिक रूप से घना प्रकाशन काल जिसने औरोबिंदो के अलीपुर के बाद के राजनीतिक चरण को चिह्नित किया।
