shared.concept_anchor: Aurobindo Uttarpara Speech — spiritual turn criticism retreat vs reframing

en.display_text:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) regarding Aurobindo Ghosh's Uttarpara Speech of 1909:

Assertion (A): In the Uttarpara Speech, Aurobindo Ghosh declared that Indian nationalism was not merely a political enterprise but a divinely ordained mission, and that India's liberation would allow her to fulfill her civilizational destiny as the spiritual teacher of humanity.

Reason (R): Critics of Aurobindo's spiritual turn questioned whether his reframing of political struggle as divine mission represented a philosophical deepening of nationalism or a practical retreat from the organizational demands of political resistance at a critical historical juncture.

(a) Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) A is incorrect but R is correct
en.strong_distractor: a — Option a is a strong distractor because students may know both facts (Aurobindo's Uttarpara Speech announced a spiritual transformation AND critics questioned whether this represented a retreat from political struggle) and assume the criticism naturally explains and validates the speech's political significance, missing that the Reason (critics' skepticism) does not causally explain the Assertion (the speech's thesis).
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is Assertion (A) correct? — Yes. The Uttarpara Speech (1909) explicitly declared that nationalism is a divine mission and that India is destined to serve as spiritual teacher to humanity — this is Aurobindo's documented thesis.

Step 2: Is Reason (R) correct? — Yes. Critics (including secular nationalists, some Marxist historians, and contemporaries) did question whether Aurobindo's spiritual turn represented a retreat from the practical demands of political struggle at a critical juncture.

Step 3: Does R causally explain A? — No. The Assertion states what the Uttarpara Speech argued; the Reason states what critics thought about it afterward. Critics' skepticism is a response to the speech, not an explanation of why Aurobindo made the arguments he made. They are causally independent.
A correct + R correct + R does NOT explain A → option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The conflation trap presents two true facts — Aurobindo's Uttarpara thesis and critical responses to his spiritual turn — and implies a causal relationship. Students who process both as part of the same 'controversy' may assume the critical response explains the speech's political significance. In reality, the Assertion describes Aurobindo's argument, and the Reason describes the critical response — they are logically independent facts that happened to be temporally connected, not causally linked.
en.final_explanation:
The Uttarpara Speech (1909) is one of the most analyzed texts in Indian nationalist intellectual history.

Assertion (A): Correct. In the Uttarpara Speech, delivered shortly after his release from Alipore prison, Aurobindo declared that Indian nationalism is not merely a political movement but a divine mission — that India's liberation would allow her to fulfill her destiny as the world's spiritual teacher (vishwaguru). This conflation of political and spiritual liberation is the speech's central thesis.

Reason (R): Correct. Critics — including secular nationalists, later Marxist historians like R.P. Dutt, and contemporaries skeptical of religious nationalism — questioned whether Aurobindo's spiritual reframing of the nationalist struggle represented a philosophical deepening or a practical retreat from the urgent demands of political organization at a critical moment.

Causal relationship: R does not explain A. The Uttarpara Speech's arguments (A) were driven by Aurobindo's own spiritual transformation in prison and his philosophical framework — not by critics' skepticism. The critical response (R) came after the speech and reflects others' reactions to it. Two true facts; no causal connection.

This maps to option (b).

Value Addition:
• The Uttarpara Speech is sometimes paired with Aurobindo's later 1947 radio address as bookends of his vision for India — one at the beginning of his spiritual phase, one at the moment of independence.
• Gandhi also spiritualized politics but grounded his framework in ahimsa; Aurobindo grounded his in shakti and karma yoga — the contrast is philosophically fundamental.
• Partha Chatterjee uses the inner/outer domain framework to contextualize exactly this kind of spiritual-political conflation in colonial nationalist thought.

1909 में औरोबिंदो घोष के उत्तरपारा भाषण के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथन (Assertion) और कारण (Reason) पर विचार करें:

कथन (A): उत्तरपारा भाषण में, औरोबिंदो घोष ने घोषित किया कि भारतीय राष्ट्रवाद केवल एक राजनीतिक प्रयास नहीं बल्कि एक दिव्य रूप से निर्धारित मिशन है, और भारत की मुक्ति उसे मानवता के आध्यात्मिक शिक्षक के रूप में अपनी सभ्यतागत नियति पूरी करने की अनुमति देगी।

कारण (R): औरोबिंदो के आध्यात्मिक परिवर्तन के आलोचकों ने सवाल किया कि क्या उनके राजनीतिक संघर्ष को दिव्य मिशन के रूप में पुनःपरिभाषित करना राष्ट्रवाद की दार्शनिक गहराई है या एक महत्वपूर्ण ऐतिहासिक मोड़ पर राजनीतिक प्रतिरोध की संगठनात्मक मांगों से व्यावहारिक पीछे हटना है।

(a) A और R दोनों सही हैं, और R, A की सही व्याख्या है
(b) A और R दोनों सही हैं, परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
(c) A सही है परंतु R गलत है

कथन (A): सही। उत्तरपारा भाषण में, जो अलिपोर जेल से रिहाई के तुरंत बाद दिया गया, औरोबिंदो ने घोषित किया कि भारतीय राष्ट्रवाद केवल एक राजनीतिक आंदोलन नहीं बल्कि एक दिव्य मिशन है — कि भारत की मुक्ति उसे विश्व का आध्यात्मिक शिक्षक (विश्वगुरु) बनने का भाग्य पूरा करने देगी। राजनीतिक और आध्यात्मिक मुक्ति का यह सम्मिश्रण भाषण का केंद्रीय सिद्धांत है।
